items.text:
Alcaraz beat Medvedev for the 8th time in 11 meetings, 6–2, 6–4 in the group stage. Alcaraz won 7 games in a row from 1–2 down in the first set. Alcaraz landed 56% of his first serves, compared with his 68% average on hard over the last 52 weeks, and won 74% of his first-serve points (20 of 27) and 76% of his second-serve points (16 of 21), compared with his usual 56%. His first-serve percentage is something to watch in the next round. Returning, Alcaraz won 24% of the points against the first serve (7 of 29), compared with his usual 34%. Alcaraz faced no break points. Medvedev struggled on his second serve, winning 39% of the points (7 of 18), compared with his 49% average on hard over the last 52 weeks.

Alcaraz won the first set 6-2 in 31 minutes in a very one-sided start and he went for his shots from the beginning. His returns did much of the damage, including a strong return off a big second serve from Medvedev and he kept breaking serve while covering the whole court. Medvedev looked lost, shrugging his shoulders and shaking his head as the breaks went against him. Alcaraz briefly lost focus and gave up break chances but he held on. Alcaraz preferred the faster court in Turin to the slower court at Indian Wells, where Medvedev had beaten him. He finished with a one-sided win, looked relaxed throughout and moved to two wins from two matches this week.

Physically, it is something to follow. Alcaraz took a medical timeout at 2–1 in the second set. We do not know the reason. Something to follow up for the next round.

Alcaraz: W: 16 / UE: 13 | DR: 1.53

Medvedev: W: 15 / UE: 21 | DR: 0.65

items.text:
Zverev beat Shelton in straight sets in his second group match in Turin and reached the semi-finals.

He broke Shelton in the opening game and took the first set 6–2 with a second break. The second set was closer and stayed on serve. Shelton came back from 15–40 to hold for 5–4 but Zverev was the better player in the tiebreak and took it 7–4.

Through all of it, he was only thinking about his own tennis. Zverev had not even known he needed straight sets: "No, I didn't know that, but I think for me, if I focus on myself and I play good tennis, the results will take care of themselves in a way." He played good tennis and he got the straight-sets win.

His serve did the rest. He was never broken and won 88% of his first-serve points, far above his 78% average on hard. The match was more one-sided than the tiebreak suggests.

A win that says a lot about Zverev, who focused on himself and played good tennis. It was clean and dominant, with a performance rating of 9.4, a dominance ratio of 2.14 and just 10 unforced errors and he now gets Fils in his last group match.

items.text:
Fils beat Jodar 4–6, 6–2, 6–2 in the group stage to get his first win at the ATP Finals and stay in contention for the semi-finals. It was the first appearance at this event for both players.

The first set could easily have gone the other way. Fils was the one with the break points but Jodar saved two of them early in the set and another one late. Then, in the very last game, Jodar broke to take it 6–4 and lead by a set. Fils was angry with himself for letting that set slip and the win brought him relief: "Here the first set was a bit so-so. I was struggling a little bit, a bit of frustration. … A little bit of relief now."

From there he took control. He broke early in the second set and won 5 games in a row to take it 6–2 and level at one set all. The deciding set went the same way. He got an early break, added a second one late and took it 6–2.

That turnaround came from the way he kept pressing to the end. He was clearly the better player from the baseline, hit his targets with real accuracy and kept putting Jodar's serve under pressure. Over the whole match, it added up to a dominance ratio of 1.66.

On the other side of the net, Jodar called the physio in the middle of the second set.

That is a good win with one clear thing to fix. Fils landed only 50% of his first serves, well below his 63% average on hard and he will need more of them in his last group match. Up next: Zverev.

Fils: performance rating 8.8 | W: 18 / UE: 19 | DR: 1.66

Jodar: performance rating 7.6 | W: 20 / UE: 33 | DR: 0.60

Medvedev beat Cobolli 7–6, 6–3 in Turin to end the first appearance of Cobolli at this event, which he played at home.

All of that rested on his serve. Medvedev did not face a single break point all match. Even his second serve held up, with 69% of the points won against his usual 50%.

Ho acquisito più esperienza. Ogni volta che gioco su questa superficie acquisisco anche sicurezza. Sono davvero felice di dimostrare a tutti che qui riesco a giocare un ottimo tennis. Posso tenere testa a chiunque con servizi e colpi potenti, piatti, ed essere in grado di vincere quel tipo di partite. Sono semplicemente felice di vedere che sto raggiungendo il livello che ho sempre pensato di poter raggiungere

items.text:
Alcaraz beat Tiafoe in straight sets in Turin in just 68 minutes. It was the first appearance of Tiafoe at this event and he faced an opponent who was close to his best from the very first game.

Alcaraz broke him at once and broke again early on to take the first set 6–2. The second set followed the same path. Alcaraz got the early break and then met the only real danger of the match: Tiafoe had three break points. Alcaraz saved all three and held. He broke once more, served it out and took the set 6–2.

That control came from a very complete game. Alcaraz switched direction easily from cross-court to down the line and chose the right moment to speed up a rally. He did most of his damage with the forehand. On return he won 100% of the points against Tiafoe's second serve, far above his usual 54%. He felt that every part of his game was there: "The knee? I'm taking care of it, for now I'm moving well … Today I felt like everything was working for me". Tiafoe could stay with him only in short flashes of touch.

Overall, Tiafoe's one real chance came and went with those three break points and after that the match was gone. It was a clean, dominant win, with a performance rating of 9.6, a dominance ratio of 2.06 and just 9 unforced errors. Next is Medvedev.

items.text:
Shelton beat Fils in three sets at the ATP Finals in Turin, his first ever match win at this event. It was also the first appearance here for Fils and he made Shelton fight all the way to a deciding set.

From the start Shelton was the stronger player. Fils had to save 4 break points just to hold early on and the breaks came soon after that. Shelton won 5 games in a row to take the first set 6–2 and lead by a set. The second set went the other way. Fils broke late, served for the set and held on to take it 6–3 for one set all.

That left everything to the third set and Fils came into it slowly. He knew it and was not happy with himself: "It's a shame that I started the third set with the handbrake slightly on … I'm staying positive ahead of the next matches" Shelton made him pay right away. He needed 4 break points in the opening return game but got the break for 2–0. A few games later Fils had 2 chances to break back. Shelton saved both and held for 4–1. He stayed calm when he served for the match, saved one more break point and took the set 6–3.

68% behind his second serve, against his 53% average on hard, says how much his serve carried him. He mixed big serves into the body with wide ones. He also won more points than Fils in both the short and the long rallies. The match was more one-sided than the score. Fils kept it close by saving most of the break points he faced. It was not perfect: Shelton made 32 unforced errors, many of them on the backhand.

Shelton won this match early in the deciding set, with a break he had to fight for and a serve that held every time Fils pushed in that set. Credit to him. He plays Zverev next.

Shelton: performance rating 8.8 | W: 28 / UE: 32 | DR: 1.37

Fils: performance rating 8.1 | W: 21 / UE: 22 | DR: 0.73

items.text:
Zverev beat Jodar in straight sets in the opening singles match of the week in Turin. It was the first appearance at this event for Jodar, who is only 20.

The first set stayed even until the middle. Jodar saved two break points to hold and Zverev broke him soon after. Then Zverev served for the set and fell behind 15–40 but he saved both break points and took it 6–4. The second set followed the same pattern. Zverev broke early and did not see another break point. Jodar saved three more break points late in the set to stay close but Zverev served it out 6–4. Jodar afterwards: "He handled the important points better than I did … I don't feel pressure, I try to enjoy it as much as possible"

The score was kinder to Jodar than the match itself, because he kept it close only by saving 5 of 7 break points. Jodar never got a real look at the first serve. Zverev won 86% of the points behind it, far above his 74% average on hard.

A very good start to the week from Zverev, a clean and dominant win with a dominance ratio of 2.01. He handled the important points better than the young debutant and was never in real danger. Shelton waits next.

Zverev: W: 21 / UE: 18 | DR: 2.01

Jodar: W: 12 / UE: 10 | DR: 0.50

Jodar, aged 20 and making his debut at the event, came through his first two service games well but his serve was named as an area where he can still improve. The ball was not flying through the air and the players seemed to struggle at times to control it. Zverev served big and posted a high first serve percentage, taking the first set after 40 minutes. The second set followed a similar pattern. Jodar's movement and athleticism were good enough to compete at this level but Zverev's serving proved a little too much for him.
